title: DINO-X: A Unified Vision Model for Open-World Object Detection and Understanding

problem.summary: Text-prompt-only open-set detectors cannot cover long-tailed detection scenarios because sufficiently diverse training data is hard to collect, and text-only encoders limit multimodal alignment needed for open-world detection.
statements: Traditional text-prompt-only open-set detectors fail to cover a sufficient range of long-tailed detection scenarios due to the difficulty of collecting sufficiently diverse training data.
A text-only encoder such as BERT is trained solely on text data, which limits effectiveness for perception tasks requiring multimodal alignment like open-world detection.
Users often cannot describe target objects with text alone, leaving detection scenarios uncovered when only text prompts are supported.

evidence.quote: Traditional text prompt-only models [33, 47, 29], while having made great progress, still struggle to cover a sufficient range of long-tailed detection scenarios due to the difficulty of collecting sufficiently diverse training data to cover various applications.
the BERT model is trained solely on text data, which limits its effectiveness for perception tasks requiring multimodal alignment, such as open-world detection.

background.summary: DINO-X builds directly on Grounding DINO 1.5/1.6's Transformer encoder-decoder open-set detector, T-Rex2's visual prompting, and Mask DINO/Mask2Former mask decoding, claiming to unify them into one object-centric model with stronger long-tail grounding.

relatedWork.name: Grounding DINO 1.5
relatedWork.relation: direct architectural base and main prior system
relatedWork.quote: DINO-X employs the same Transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture as Grounding DINO 1.5 [47] to pursue an object-level representation for open-world object understanding.

relatedWork.name: T-Rex2
relatedWork.relation: source of the visual prompt encoder and visual-prompt training data
relatedWork.quote: DINO-X also supports visual prompts as in T-Rex2 [18], further covering detection scenarios that cannot be well described by text alone.

relatedWork.name: Mask DINO
relatedWork.relation: design basis for the segmentation mask head
relatedWork.quote: Following the core design of Mask2Former [4] and Mask DINO [28], we construct the pixel embedding map by fusing the 1/4 resolution backbone feature and the upsampled 1/8 resolution feature from the Transformer encoder.

evidence.quote: Building upon Grounding DINO 1.5 [47], DINO-X employs the same Transformer encoder-decoder architecture and adopts open-set detection as its core training task.

solution.summary: DINO-X is a unified object-centric Transformer detector pre-trained on a new 100M-image grounding dataset (Grounding-100M) that accepts text, visual, and customized prompts and attaches multiple perception heads for boxes, masks, keypoints, and language outputs, with a distilled Edge variant for deployment.
solution.approach: Pre-train a Grounding-DINO-style encoder-decoder on Grounding-100M with three prompt types (text, visual, customized including a universal prompt-free object prompt), then add task heads on the shared object-level representation.
components: visual prompt encoder (box/point prompts, from T-Rex2)
customized prompts via prompt-tuning, incl. a universal object prompt for prompt-free detection
language-guided query selection box head with L1 + G-IoU and contrastive losses
mask head (1/4 + 1/8 resolution features, sampled-point mask loss)
keypoint heads for person and hand
lightweight language head (RoIAlign object tokens + autoregressive decoder)
Edge variant with EfficientViT backbone, Pro-to-Edge knowledge distillation, FP16 quantization

evidence.quote: we develop a universal object prompt to support prompt-free open-world object detection, making it possible to detect any objects in a given image without requiring users to provide any prompt.
To achieve a strong grounding performance, we collected and curated over 100 million high-quality grounding samples from diverse sources, termed as Grounding-100M.
DINO-X performs deep feature fusion between the prompt and the visual features extracted from the input image and then apply different heads for different perception tasks.

experiments.summary: The paper evaluates zero-shot detection/segmentation on COCO and LVIS, visual-prompt counting on FSC147/FSCD-LVIS, pose on COCO/CrowdPose/Human-Art/HInt, and region understanding on LVIS/PACO/Visual Genome, plus speed for the Edge model on A100 and Orin NX.

evidence.quote: the DINO-X Pro model achieves 56.0 AP, 59.8 AP, and 52.4 AP on the COCO, LVIS-minival, and LVIS-val zero-shot object detection benchmarks, respectively.
DINO-X Edge also achieves 48.3 AP and 42.0 AP on LVIS-minival and LVIS-val, respectively, demonstrating excellent zero-shot detection capability in long-tailed detection scenarios.
an inference speed of 20.1 FPS, marking a 33% improvement compared to Grounding DINO 1.6 Edge (increasing from 15.1 FPS to 20.1 FPS).

limitations.summary: The unified model still trails a detection-plus-SAM pipeline on instance segmentation, its pose head underperforms ED-Pose due to few trainable parameters, and it lags Osprey on part-level recognition; the dense region caption feature is unfinished.
items: Instance segmentation quality remains behind the Grounded SAM assembly, reflecting the difficulty of training one model for multiple tasks.
Pose head reaches 1.6 AP below ED-Pose, attributed to the limited number of trainable parameters.
Object recognition on PACO is inferior to Osprey, possibly due to training-data discrepancy.
Dense region caption / region-based QA is still in development and not yet released.

evidence.quote: Compared to Grounded SAM, there is still a notable performance gap for DINO-X to catch up, which shows the challenge of training a unified model for multiple tasks.
While our model achieves an AP that is 1.6 lower than ED-Pose (primarily due to the limited number of trainable parameters in the pose head), it outperforms existing models on CrowdPose and Human-Art
On the PACO dataset, our model is inferior to Osprey.

futureDirections.direction: Further optimize the mask head to close the instance-segmentation gap.
futureDirections.quote: We will further optimize the performance of the mask head in our future work.

futureDirections.direction: Ship the dense region caption / region-based QA capability in the next model version.
futureDirections.quote: Currently, this feature is still in the development stage and will be released in our next version.

applications.detail: Open-set detection is claimed to enhance robot adaptability in dynamic environments.
applications.quote: enhancing the adaptability of robots in dynamic environments

applications.detail: Open-set detection is claimed to help autonomous vehicles locate and react to new objects quickly.
applications.quote: assisting autonomous vehicles in rapidly locating and reacting to new objects

applications.detail: Prompt-free detection is suggested to expand applications such as screen parsing.
applications.quote: thereby expanding its potential applications in areas such as screen parsing [35], etc.

deploymentClaims: DINO-X Edge is optimized for faster inference and better suited for deployment on edge devices.
20.1 FPS at 640x640 input, a 33% speedup over Grounding DINO 1.6 Edge (15.1 FPS), with FP16 quantization that does not sacrifice performance.
FP16 quantization raises Edge speed from 10.7 FPS to 20.1 FPS versus Grounding DINO 1.5 Edge.
A public demo and API are released at https://github.com/IDEA-Research/DINO-X-API.

evidence.quote: which is optimized for faster inference speed and better suited for deployment on edge devices.
Leveraging the normalization technique in floating-point multiplication, we can quantize the model to FP16 without sacrificing the performance.
